description: Machine-readable guidance for using Kineto next to popular UI libraries and design systems, and for AI tools (Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, Figma MCP flows) that decide which Kineto module fits a piece of UI. Every module, variant and option named here is validated against kineto.features.json by tests/integrations-contract.mjs. Human-readable docs under docs/integrations/ and the AI rule files under ai/ are generated from this file — edit here, then run `npm run integrations:build`.
principles: Kineto adds motion and media effects to markup you already own; it does not replace the component library's behaviour (dialogs, menus, forms, routing).

Prefer the library's own component when it already provides the behaviour (toast, tooltip, tabs, accordion, dialog, carousel). Use Kineto for what the library does not ship: entrance motion, text motion, counters, image loading effects, hover/pointer effects, marquee, page reveal, cursor, scroll storytelling.

Never put two things that animate the same property on one element: a Tailwind/tw-animate-css enter animation plus a Kineto reveal, a Bootstrap carousel plus a Kineto slider, two Kineto modules that both write transform (see docs/rfc/module-composition.md).

Attach with `data-kt-*` attributes on the element that reaches the DOM, call `Kineto.observe()` once at startup so markup added later (framework renders, portals, modals) is picked up and cleaned up, and reach for the React/Vue adapters only when you need the instance (replay, pause, presence).
Respect `prefers-reduced-motion`: Kineto already renders the meaningful end state for every module, so do not add a second reduced-motion branch around it.
Read the exact option names from kineto.features.json (or `npx @dong-gri/kineto-mcp`); do not invent options.

setup.bootstrapScript:
import Kineto from '@dong-gri/kineto';
Kineto.observe(); // scans now and follows later DOM changes

vanilla.title: Vanilla HTML / CSS

attach.summary: Put `data-kt-<module>="<variant>"` and `data-kt-<option>` attributes on the element. Call `Kineto.observe()` (or `Kineto.autoInit()` for static pages) once.
attach.example: Headline

notes: Every Kineto module is available; there is no library component to defer to.
Multi-page sites can add `data-kt-page-transition` on <body> for same-origin page transitions and `data-kt-page-reveal` for the first-paint overlay.

shadcn.title: shadcn/ui (Radix / Base UI + Tailwind)

attach.summary: shadcn components spread extra props onto their root DOM node, so `data-kt-*` props reach the DOM unchanged. Add `<KinetoProvider>` (registry item `@kineto/provider`) once in the root layout; it imports the stylesheet and calls `Kineto.observe()` on the client. Use `useKineto` / `<Motion>` from `@dong-gri/kineto/react` only when the code needs the instance.

conflicts: tw-animate-css (`animate-in`, `fade-in-0`, `zoom-in-95` …) already animates Dialog/Sheet/Popover content — do not add a Kineto reveal to the same node; animate the children instead.
shadcn `Carousel` (Embla) owns the track; put Kineto reveal/tilt on the slides, never `data-kt-slider` on the same container.
shadcn `Skeleton` is a layout placeholder; for images prefer `data-kt-lazy="skeleton"` on the `` itself so the placeholder resolves into the real picture.
notes: Next.js App Router: the provider is a client component; server components can still render `data-kt-*` attributes.
Tailwind v4 utilities and Kineto never fight over layout: Kineto only writes transform/opacity/filter/clip on the host and creates its own wrapper layers.

tailwind.title: Tailwind CSS (no component library)

attach.summary: Same as vanilla: `data-kt-*` attributes on utility-styled markup. Keep Tailwind `transition-*`/`animate-*` classes off elements that carry a Kineto reveal/gesture.
attach.example: <article class="rounded-2xl bg-white p-6 shadow" data-kt-reveal="fade-up" data-kt-once>…</article>

conflicts: `animate-*` keyframe utilities and `transition-transform` on the same element as `data-kt-reveal`, `data-kt-gesture` or `data-kt-tilt` double-animate the host.
notes: daisyUI, Flowbite and Preline are plain class-based markup on top of Tailwind; everything in this entry applies to them.

bootstrap.title: Bootstrap 5

attach.summary: `data-bs-*` (Bootstrap) and `data-kt-*` (Kineto) live on the same element without conflict. Load Bootstrap's bundle and Kineto's UMD (or ESM) and call `Kineto.observe()`; toasts, popovers and dynamically shown modals are picked up automatically.
attach.example: …

conflicts: `.carousel` (Bootstrap) and `data-kt-slider` on the same element: choose one. Bootstrap carousel for content slides, Kineto slider when you want coverflow/cube/cards effects.
`.placeholder` / `.placeholder-glow` and `data-kt-lazy="skeleton"`: choose one placeholder per image.
`data-bs-toggle="tooltip"` and `data-kt-tooltip` on one element create two tooltips.
`.accordion` (Bootstrap collapse) and `data-kt-accordion`: Bootstrap owns open/close; add Kineto reveal to the panel content instead.

examples.title: Bootstrap 5 coexistence page — modal, toast, tooltip, carousel, cards and KPI counters with Kineto attached, plus the conflict rules applied.

notes: Bootstrap's `.fade` modal transition stays; animate the modal body with `data-kt-reveal` or `data-kt-text-split` for richer entrances.
Bootstrap's grid and utilities are unaffected; Kineto never sets layout properties on the host.

mui.title: Material UI (MUI)

attach.summary: MUI components forward unknown props (including `data-kt-*`) and refs to their root element. Mount `<KinetoProvider>` once, then add attributes on `Card`, `Button`, `Typography`, `Box` …

conflicts: MUI `Grow`/`Fade`/`Slide` transitions wrap Dialog and Menu content; do not add a Kineto reveal to the same node.
MUI `ButtonBase` already renders a Material ripple (`TouchRipple`); use `data-kt-magnetic` or `data-kt-gesture` on buttons, not `data-kt-ripple`.
notes: Emotion class names are left untouched; Kineto writes inline styles it later restores on destroy.

mantine.title: Mantine

attach.summary: Mantine components spread `...others` onto the root node and forward refs, so `data-kt-*` props work everywhere. Mount `<KinetoProvider>` once.

conflicts: `@mantine/carousel` (Embla) and `data-kt-slider` on one element: choose one.
Mantine `Transition`/`Collapse` already animate their child; add Kineto to the content, not the transition node.

chakra.title: Chakra UI v3

attach.summary: Chakra v3 components are Ark UI + style props; unknown `data-kt-*` props reach the DOM. Mount `<KinetoProvider>` once. For `asChild` compositions put the attribute on the element that renders.

conflicts: Chakra `Presence`/`Dialog` animate their positioner via `data-state` keyframes; do not add a Kineto reveal to the same node.

antd.title: Ant Design

attach.summary: Most Ant Design components pass extra HTML attributes to their root (`Button`, `Card`, `Typography.Title`, `Statistic` wrapper). When a component does not forward `data-kt-*` (check the rendered DOM), wrap it in a plain `<div data-kt-…>` or use `useKineto` with a `ref`. Mount `<KinetoProvider>` once.
attach.example: import { Card, Statistic } from 'antd'; 128,000

conflicts: Ant Design `Carousel` (react-slick) and `data-kt-slider` on one element: choose one.
`Statistic` has its own count-up animation when `formatter` uses CountUp; use either that or `data-kt-counter`, not both.

daisyui.title: daisyUI

attach.summary: daisyUI is CSS classes only, so attach exactly like vanilla HTML. daisyUI ships static `skeleton`, `toast`, `tooltip`, `tabs` and `collapse` classes without JavaScript; Kineto can supply the behaviour where you need motion or live state.

conflicts: daisyUI `carousel` is CSS scroll-snap; `data-kt-slider` on the same element takes over the track — choose one.
notes: daisyUI `skeleton` boxes stay for text; use `data-kt-lazy="skeleton"` on images.

nuxt-ui.title: Nuxt UI (Reka UI + Tailwind)

attach.summary: Vue attribute fallthrough puts `data-kt-*` on the component's root element. Register a client plugin (`plugins/kineto.client.ts`) that imports the stylesheet and calls `Kineto.observe()`; use `v-motion` / `useKineto` from `@dong-gri/kineto/vue` when you need the instance.
attach.example:
…

Nuxt launch

conflicts: Nuxt UI `UCarousel` (Embla) and `data-kt-slider`: choose one per container.
Reka UI content nodes animate through `data-state`; add Kineto to their children.
notes: Components rendered on the server keep the attributes, so hydration sees the same markup the observer will scan.

primevue.title: PrimeVue v4

attach.summary: PrimeVue components fall attributes through to the root (or accept `pt` pass-through for inner parts). `Dialog`, `Toast` and `Sidebar` teleport to `<body>`, which `Kineto.observe()` on the document already covers.

conflicts: PrimeVue `Carousel`/`Galleria` and `data-kt-slider` on the same element: choose one.
PrimeVue `Ripple` directive and `data-kt-ripple` on one button: choose one.

vuetify.title: Vuetify 3

attach.summary: Vuetify components pass `data-kt-*` attributes to their root element. Register a plugin that calls `Kineto.observe()` after the app mounts; overlays (`v-dialog`, `v-snackbar`) render into the overlay container and are observed like any other DOM.

conflicts: `v-carousel` and `data-kt-slider` on one element: choose one.
`v-btn` already has a ripple; use `data-kt-magnetic`/`data-kt-gesture` instead of `data-kt-ripple`.

recipes.why: Characters resolve left to right — the default look for launch pages.
Korean copy: assembles jamo into syllables instead of flashing random glyphs.
Word-by-word rise for editorial headlines.
Game/tech key art: RGB slice burst on the title.
Blurred lines sharpen into place — soft, editorial headlines.

intents.title: Section / card entrance on scroll

recipes.why: Default entrance for sections and cards.
Editorial mask wipe for images and quotes.
Designer-owned CSS: Kineto only toggles the class, the stylesheet animates.
Colour block wipes across an image or heading.

notes: For lists, add `data-kt-stagger` on the parent so children cascade instead of animating each item separately.

intents.title: Card hover: tilt, glow, spring

recipes.why: Pointer-following 3D tilt with a glare; showcase and product cards.
Spotlight that follows the pointer inside the card (works on dark UIs).
Luminous gradient border for pricing/feature cards.
Subtle spring lift for dense lists where 3D would be noisy.

notes: Pick one transform-writing module per element (tilt, gesture, magnetic all write transform).

intents.title: Call-to-action button feedback

recipes.why: Button leans toward the pointer; landing-page CTAs.
Click ripple for libraries without one (Bootstrap, daisyUI, Nuxt UI).
Hover/press spring for any button.
Haptic tap on supported mobile devices (progressive).

notes: Skip `ripple` where the library button already ripples (MUI, Vuetify, PrimeVue).

recipes.why: Slot-machine reels for dashboard stats.
Final digits land one by one — hero stats.
Plain count-up for ratings and small numbers.
Countdown to a launch/event date.
"3 minutes ago" style relative time from a server date.

intents.title: Image loading effect / placeholder

recipes.why: Shimmer placeholder that resolves into the image.
Blurred preview sharpening — content sites.
Stepped pixel mosaic settling into the image — editorial/product shots.

notes: Library skeletons are layout boxes for text; Kineto's lazy skeleton sits on the `` and hands off to the real picture with no layout shift.

intents.title: Graphic texture on an image or video

recipes.why: Retro two-tone dither kept on the image (brand/showcase).
Dither that shrinks into the original photo once it scrolls into view.
The dither to reach for on a photograph: `noise` has no repeating tile, so a fine cell reads as texture instead of as an 8x8 weave. Use this before reaching for a smaller cell size.
Clustered-dot print screen: ink grows as one blob per cell, the way newsprint and risograph do. Keep the cell small (1-3px) or the blobs read as a checkerboard.
Newspaper halftone. The angle is the part that matters: a screen square to the frame reads as a table, and tilting it 15-45 degrees is what makes it read as print.
Open-ring screen: thin outlines in the highlights that close up in the shadows. A graphic, editorial texture rather than a photographic one.
A dither that stays on the image while the grain crawls — alive without moving the layout.
ASCII that keeps re-typing itself: the living-terminal look for a hero or an about page.
The picture sharpens only under the pointer — an interaction, not just a filter.
Permanent halftone print look on an image or video.
ASCII-art filter for terminal/tech aesthetics.
Chromatic-aberration glitch bursts over a photo — louder than a texture.

notes: Raise `contrast` (1.3-1.6) before anything else: a photograph sits in the middle of the tonal range and dithers to grey mush at the default 1.

Pick `ditherType` by the subject, not by taste: `noise` for a photograph (no repeating tile, so a fine cell reads as texture), `cluster` or a rotated `halftone` for a print look, `8x8`/`16x16` for a graphic two-tone treatment, and `floyd-steinberg`/`atkinson` when the original colours have to survive.
Stylize redraws the pixels; it does not load anything. Pair it with the `image-loading` intent when the picture also needs lazy loading — both attributes can sit on one .
A source the canvas cannot read back (cross-origin without CORS) simply shows unstyled, so the texture is never a hard dependency.

`motion` (drift/shuffle/scan/flow/pulse) keeps the look alive on a still picture and `pointer` (lens/spotlight/ripple) makes it react; both redraw every frame, so lower `renderFps` when several are on one screen.

recipes.why: Grouped viewer with zoom, pan, minimap and keyboard navigation.
Pointer/touch brush uncovers the image — event pages and scratch cards.
Automatic cover wipe when no interaction is wanted.

One-shot entrance for the modal body when the library only fades the overlay.
Full-screen takeover transitions (showcase/event sites).

Multi-page sites: fetch same-origin pages and animate between them.
Full-screen loader bound to real load progress.

Hide on scroll down, show on scroll up.

Terminal-style frames for developer/AI products.
Full-screen loader bound to fetch/promise/resource progress.

Rotating text ring over hoverable media.
Image or sprite cursor (must be same-origin for demos).

recipes.why: Confetti burst on a button or when a section enters view.

Figma's corner smoothing and iOS icons are superellipses, not circles. `border-radius` alone cannot draw one, and CSS `corner-shape` is Chromium-only — this uses it there and draws the same curve everywhere else.
A straight diagonal cut, for ticket stubs, tags and cut-corner panels.
A square bite out of each corner, for coupon and stamp shapes.
Destructive actions confirmed by holding the button.

recipes.why: `<details>`-based accordion with animated height.
WAI-ARIA tabs with a sliding indicator.
Form-connected toggle switch.

deprecations.why: Lazy fetches an image; these redraw pixels that are already there. They are the Stylize module now, and Stylize adds the living look (motion, pointer) and the crisp dissolve reveal that the alias cannot reach.

figmaHints.description: How to map a Figma node (via the Figma MCP `get_design_context` / `get_metadata`) to an intent. Match node names case-insensitively against `figma` patterns of each intent; then use the node type as a tiebreaker.

nodeTypeRules.when: node is a TEXT layer with font size ≥ 40 or named like a heading
node is an IMAGE fill (RECTANGLE/FRAME with image paint) or named image/photo/thumbnail
node repeats as a grid/list of similar frames (auto-layout children with the same component)
node is a COMPONENT INSTANCE named Button/CTA
node text is mostly digits (counts, KRW/USD, percentages)
frame is wider than the viewport and clips horizontally repeating children
frame has prototype interaction 'On drag' or scroll horizontally

workflow: Read the frame with the Figma MCP and list its top-level layers.
For each layer, match names against the intents' `figma` patterns and the node type rules above.
Build the layer with the project's component library first (shadcn, Bootstrap, …).

Add the Kineto attribute from the matching intent's first recipe unless the ecosystem's `provides` list already covers that behaviour (then prefer the library component and only add motion to its content).
Never add more than one transform-writing module per element; prefer one reveal per section rather than per element.
